newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-GRAF AND SELES FACE HURDLES TO OPEN FINAL.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-GRAF AND SELES FACE HURDLES TO OPEN FINAL.

text.p: Steffi Graf and Monica Seles are a step away from a Grand Slam reunion, but a former Wimbledon champion and the brightest young star in tennis stand in the way of a U.S. Open final showdown.
Graf meets 15-year-old Swiss sensation Martina Hingis, while Seles takes on Spain's Conchita Martinez, the 1994 Wimbledon champion, in the women's semifinals on Friday.

Seles returned to the Grand Slam stage at last year's Open after missing more than two-and-half-years following a stabbing attack in Hamburg and completed a breathtaking charge into the final before falling to Graf in three sets.
Top-seeded Graf and second seed Seles -- ranked co-world number ones all year -- looked likely to launch a lively renewal of their rivalry. But they have not squared off since.
Aiming to play the role of spoiler in this Grand Slam melodrama are the veteran Martinez and the precocious Hingis.

The carefree Hingis will be swinging from the heels and belting away from the baseline, while Martinez hopes a new edge of aggressiveness will help her break through against Seles, who has won all eight of their previous encounters.
Hingis already has one of only three wins registered this season against Graf, beating the German in the quarters of the Italian Open. Graf gained revenge at Wimbledon.
"I have nothing to lose against her," Hingis said about meeting Graf.

Hingis, who lost about seven pounds (3.5 kg) in a conditioning programme this summer, surprised third seed Arantxa Sanchez Vicario of Spain in the fourth round before ousting seventh-seeded Czech Jana Novotna in the quarters.
Graf leads their head-to-head series 3-1.
"She seems to believe a lot more in herself and believes she can play and win against the top players and she is playing a little bit more aggressive which definitely helps her game," said Graf.
"I am a little disappointed about the way I am playing," conceded Graf after beating Austrian Judith Wiesner in the quarters. "I am trying to focus and it just doesn't seem to always happen."
Graf has more on her mind than her tennis opponents these days. Her father, Peter, a former used car salesman, began his trial on tax evasion charges on Thursday in Mannheim, Germany.

Having spent 13 months in investigative custody, Peter Graf faces a possible 10-year jail sentence if convicted of evading 19 million marks ($13 million) in taxes from Steffi's earnings during the late 1980s.

Seles, who romped past unseeded South African Amanda Coetzer in the quarters, knows the type of game she can expect from Martinez, who has won only two sets from Seles. The two also met last year in the semis, with Seles winning 6-2 6-2.
"She has a good first serve and she has a great forehand, so I'm going to try to stay away from that," said Seles, whose own service game has been weakened by a shoulder injury.
She doesn't make too many unforced errors. I have to hit a lot of winners. If they're in, great. If they're not, then I'm in trouble."
Martinez, who beat Linda Wild to reach the semifinals, has been putting herself into trouble of sorts to get herself into the proper mood for her matches.
The Spaniard is driving herself to the tennis centre through the challenging New York City traffic to get her adrenalin flowing and put her into an aggressive mood.
She thinks a lack of aggression has held her back in the past.
"I remember the match well," Martinez said about last year's loss to Seles. "She played well, but I didn't play good at all. I wasn't passing, wasn't aggressive enough.
"I don't think she's unbeatable at all," added Martinez. "If I play a good match, I have my chances."
